cards.text: Zechariah, a prophet, is bringing God's people a message from the LORD (Zechariah 1:1). And it opens with something every farmer cares about. Rain in springtime.

cards.question: Zechariah tells the people to ask someone for rain in springtime. Who?

cards.text: The LORD makes the storm clouds. He'll give everyone showers of rain and crops in the field. Then Zechariah brings up two other voices: idols and diviners.

cards.question: True or false: Zechariah says idols and diviners give the people real comfort.

cards.text: Idols speak deceit. Diviners tell false dreams and offer empty comfort. That's the dead batteries I shared a drawer with, swearing every single day, "I still got a little charge left!" Friend. You did NOT.

cards.question: With idols and diviners guiding them, the people wander like sheep, oppressed for lack of a ___.

cards.text: Now the LORD Himself speaks. And He's talking about the shepherds and the leaders. Oh, friend. The whole room just got quiet.

cards.question: The LORD says His anger burns against the shepherds. What does He say He'll do to the leaders?

cards.text: Because the LORD of Hosts attends to His flock, the house of Judah. And He's got big plans for these sheep.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll make His flock, the house of Judah, like what?

cards.text: A SHEEP. Into a WARHORSE. That's me going from the back of a junk drawer to running a whole bakery! Then the LORD lists what's coming: the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow and every ruler together.

cards.question: The LORD says the cornerstone will come from ___.

cards.text: They'll be like mighty men in battle, trampling the enemy in the mire of the streets. They'll put the HORSEMEN to shame. Friend, the last thing I put to shame was a rubber band in a stretching contest back in the drawer. And I don't even have arms.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says they'll fight because the LORD is with them.

cards.text: The LORD keeps going, and now He widens the circle. He'll strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll restore Judah and Joseph. What reason does He give?

cards.text: And they'll be as though He had not rejected them. Friend, I got slid to the back of a junk drawer for YEARS. Getting pulled out like it never happened? I'd be crying into the dough.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD promises He will answer them.

cards.text: Next up, Ephraim, the people who came from Joseph's son Ephraim (Genesis 41:52). Ephraim will be like a mighty man, their hearts glad as with wine. But that joy isn't staying with them.

cards.question: Ephraim's ___ will see it and be joyful, and their hearts will rejoice in the LORD.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll whistle for them to gather. A WHISTLE. That's it! No group chat. No seventeen reminder texts. One whistle, and everybody comes.

cards.question: The LORD says why He'll whistle for His people to gather. What does He say?

cards.text: They'll be as numerous as they once were. Even though the LORD sows them among the nations, scattered out into distant lands.

cards.question: True or false: Out in those distant lands, the LORD says His people will forget Him.

cards.text: They'll remember Him, and they and their children will live and return. The LORD will bring them back from Egypt, gather them from Assyria, and bring them to Gilead and Lebanon.

cards.question: The LORD will bring His people to Gilead and Lebanon until no more ___ is found for them.

cards.text: No more ROOM! Friend, I once lost a standoff with a twist tie over one inch of drawer. On the way home, they'll pass through the sea of distress and strike the waves, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up.

cards.question: Egypt and Assyria come up again. What does the LORD say happens to them?

answers.text: Assyria's pride falls and Egypt's scepter departs
Assyria and Egypt join Israel's army
Assyria and Egypt rebuild their thrones

cards.question: The LORD's last promise is that He'll strengthen His people in the LORD. Then what will they do?

findings.problem: The card says the LORD's message to Zechariah 'opens with' rain in springtime. That message began back in Zechariah 1:1. Rain is how this passage opens, not how the message opens, so the line isn't true as worded.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question already says 'His anger burns against the shepherds.' That makes 'Reward them' and 'Forgive them' easy to rule out. Neither one works as a real option.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'House of Judah' first appears on this card, but the card never says simply who Judah is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'A SHEEP. Into a WARHORSE.' changes the text's 'like His royal steed in battle' into a real transformation. It drops 'like' and renames 'royal steed' as 'warhorse.'
The question says 'they'll fight' without naming who 'they' are. The card that set them up is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question types follow a pattern. Stop 2 runs MC, TF, FB, MC, TF, FB, MC, MC, which is a repeating cycle. It also opens with the same MC, TF, FB order as stop 1. In both stops, story cards and choice cards strictly alternate.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'The house of Joseph' first appears here, but the card never says simply who they are. Ephraim gets an introduction on card 5, but Joseph doesn't get one here.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'The LORD promises He will answer them' doesn't say who 'them' is. The question needs to name Judah and Joseph.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'But that joy isn't staying with them' suggests Ephraim's joy leaves them. Zechariah 10:7 says Ephraim's hearts will be glad and their children will rejoice too. The joy spreads to the children, but it doesn't leave Ephraim.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Even though' links 'as numerous as they once were' (10:8) to being sown among the nations (10:9). In the text, 'Though I sow them' goes with 'they will remember Me,' not with being numerous. The card adds a connection the text doesn't make.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card packs three moments into one: they remember and return with their children, God brings them back from Egypt and Assyria, and God brings them to Gilead and Lebanon.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It gives Assyria and Egypt separate fates in Bible-sounding wording ('pride falls,' 'scepter departs'). Both wrong answers use the same plain 'Assyria and Egypt...' form instead.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
